sections.content:
25,845 people

were counted on the census as "sewing machinists" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Sewing machinists sew and finish garments by hand or machine, rectify faults in manufactured textile goods and repair worn and damaged garments.

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "sewing machinists" there were more women than men (83.6% compared with 16.4%).

This means "sewing machinists" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 16.4% and women made up 83.6% of "sewing machinists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sewing machinists" included:

  • social workers
  • child and early years officers
  • health associate professionals (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "sewing machinists" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "sewing machinists", 16% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sewing machinists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sewing machinists" included:

  • market and street traders and assistants
  • launderers, dry cleaners and pressers
  • shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "sewing machinists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "sewing machinists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sewing machinists", 12.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (57.3% compared with 42.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (75.3%) than self-employed (24.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the East Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leicester, this is in the same region of the East Midlands.
